observations.observation: The page could not be retrieved; no dictionary definition was inspected.

observations.limitations: One article illustrates usage; it does not establish frequency or a categorical distinction between pesan and chat.
observations.observation: The article describes responding to a group message, says “membalas pesan,” and separately calls the app area “chat.”
observations.source_title: Cara Balas Pesan di Grup WhatsApp Tanpa Ketahuan yang Lain

observations.limitations: This supports an attested chat/obrolan usage, not a general rule that chat always means conversation or app feature.
observations.observation: The thesis labels a feature “Obrolan (chat)” and describes it as private conversation; it also uses chat in the discussion.
observations.publisher: UIN Prof. K.H. Saifuddin Zuhri Purwokerto repository

observations.limitations: A single usage example cannot establish neutral general preference or the full distribution of chat.
observations.observation: The article uses pesan for the item being replied to and chat for the WhatsApp conversation area.
observations.source_title: Cara Balas Pesan di Grup WhatsApp Tanpa Ketahuan yang Lain

observations.limitations: Dictionary evidence establishes senses, not how often the word is used in current digital communication.
observations.observation: The Kamus Bahasa Melayu entry defines mesej as a message/news/brief words to be conveyed to someone and includes a telephone-message example; another listing describes a message conveyed by phone.
observations.page_location_or_query: PRPM result for “mesej,” retrieved search result.

observations.limitations: This does not show everyday preference for digital messages. The surfaced PRPM discussion includes a user questioning whether one “hantar mesej” phrasing sounds natural, but that isolated question cannot establish contrary general usage.
observations.observation: The dictionary entry records mesej as a message to be conveyed, including a telephone example.
observations.page_location_or_query: PRPM result for “mesej,” retrieved search result.

observations.limitations: The Indonesian pesan dictionary lead failed to load; the inspected Indonesian article supports pesan in WhatsApp context but cannot substantiate the proposed cross-locale preference contrast.
observations.observation: The entry establishes mesej as a Malay word for a message, including a telephone message; no comparative evidence between Indonesian pesan and Malaysian mesej preference was inspected.
